firmĭtūdo , ĭnis, f. firmus,
I.firmness, durability, strength (less freq. than firmitas, but class.).
I. Lit.: “tanta in eis (navibus) erat firmitudo,” Caes. B. G. 3, 13, 8 ; cf.: “tanta erat operis (i. e. pontis) firmitudo,” id. ib. 4, 17, 7 : “vocis,” Auct. Her. 3, 11, 20 . —
II. Trop., firmness, constancy, stability, strength of mind: “animi,” Plaut. As. 2, 2, 54 ; cf.: “quod firmitudinem gravitatemque animi tui perspexi,” Cic. Fam. 5, 13, 3 : “quantum esset hominibus praesidii in animi firmitudine,” Caes. B. C. 3, 28, 4 : “animi,” Tac. A. 4, 8 : “in patientia firmitudinem simulans,” id. ib. 6, 46
fin.; cf. ib. 15, 62: “non quod salus ab isto data quicquam habitura sit firmitudinis,” Cic. Att. 11, 14, 2 : “haec constitutio habet firmitudinem,” id. Rep. 1, 45 : “(translationes) per se minus habeant firmitudinis,” id. Inv. 2, 19, 58 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
